title: Security: Add configurable WebSocket Origin allow-list
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Our enterprise application uses Streamlit WebSockets for application communication.

During an enterprise DAST/security assessment, the scanner tested the WebSocket Origin validation by modifying the Origin header to an unauthorized domain.

The WebSocket connection was still accepted.

For example, the legitimate request contains an approved Origin:

Origin: https://<approved-application-domain>

The DAST scanner changes this to:

Origin: https://malicious-example.com

The WebSocket connection is still established.

## Security Concern

Without strict Origin validation, an authenticated WebSocket connection may potentially be initiated from an unauthorized website.

This creates a security concern for enterprise applications where access is restricted to specific trusted domains.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Streamlit should provide a supported configuration option to define an explicit WebSocket Origin allow-list.

For example:

server.websocketAllowedOrigins = [
    "https://<approved-domain>"
]

or an equivalent configuration.

The application should reject the WebSocket upgrade when the Origin is not present in the configured allow-list.

### Current Behavior

Missing WebSocket Origin Validation

Test performed by DAST:

1. Establish normal WebSocket connection.
2. Modify the Origin header to another domain.
3. Send the WebSocket upgrade request.
4. Connection is still accepted.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit: 1.60.0
- Python: 3.12
- Deployment: Azure App Service (Linux)
- Reverse proxy: Azure Application Gateway WAF v2
- Authentication: OKTA OIDC
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

Does Streamlit currently provide a supported configuration for strict WebSocket Origin validation?

If not, could a configurable WebSocket Origin allow-list be added?

This capability is required for enterprise security/DAST compliance.
